newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 16.

text.p: There are 76 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said that while irreconcilable differences existed in Hong Kong on many policy issues, all agreed that the territory would be badly damaged if China was not granted Most Favoured Nation trading status by the United States. It was important that U.S. politicians understood that harming the territory's economy by refusing to grant MFN status to China would do Hong Kong no good, the paper said.

-- The Beijing-backed WEN WEI PO said the United States' playing of the human rights card failed again. While Washington warned every year that renewal of China's MFN status would be difficult, China has never worried because MFN was not a one-way street, and the United States has granted MFN every year.
